svg.title: Free-body diagram of a block on an incline
svg.desc: A free-body diagram for a block at rest on a thirty-degree incline. A single dot stands for the block, and every force the environment exerts on it acts at that dot. The weight, 10.0 newtons, points straight down and is the longest arrow. The normal force, 8.7 newtons, points away from the surface at right angles to it. The rope's pull, 2.0 newtons, and friction, 3.0 newtons, both point up the slope, so they are drawn just to either side of the dot rather than one on top of the other; that sideways shift is a drawing convention to keep both readable and does not mean they act anywhere else. A dashed line through the dot marks the chosen axis, parallel to the incline. Only whole forces are drawn: the weight appears once, and its components along and across the slope are not drawn beside it. The four forces add to zero, which is why the block stays at rest. Illustrative data.
svg.text: forces in newtons; same-direction forces are drawn side by side
Every force on the block, drawn whole, acting at one dot
The four add to zero, which is what holding the block at rest means.
